thread:
ana: Heads-up: after the egress LB tweak last night APAC GPU pools are showing slow, persistent queue_pressure and batch_window_seconds drift. 99p token latency is spiking intermittently.

mike: Which grafana panel are you looking at? pls paste link.

ana: Fleet -> Capacity -> Pool headroom (abbrev view). link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/fleet/capacity-overview?var-region=apac
Screenshot shows apac-gpu-pool-a and apac-gpu-pool-b with rising queue_pressure but throughput steady.

sre-bot: Alert fired: GPU_POOL_EGRESS_ERRORS (apac-gpu-pool-a) at 2025-08-18T04:12:03Z :rotating_light:

jordyn: saw the alert. LB logs show a handful of 502/504s around the same time windows. correlating with client-side retries.

kai: That pattern often expands batch windows: retries pile up in the queue, runtime bundles more requests -> bigger batches -> tail latency up. Could be transient TCP resets or keepalive timeouts.

devon: Can you share the PromQL used in the headroom panel? want to reproduce in my local Prometheus.

ana: Panel query (current, simplified):
```
sum(gpu_request_queue_length) by (pool)
```
But it's deceptive. aggregate hides per-pod spikes. We should compute per-pod p95/p99 and use max_over_time for short bursts.

jordyn: Proposed recording rule and panel changes:
1) recording rule per pod p99 using histogram_quantile over gpu_queue_buckets
```
- record: pod:gpu_queue_p99:rate5m
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (pod, le) (rate(gpu_queue_buckets[5m])))
```
2) pool saturation metric: pool:gpu_saturation:ratio
```
- record: pool:gpu_saturation:ratio
  expr: sum by (pool) (rate(gpu_active_seconds[1m])) / sum by (pool) (gpu_capacity_seconds)
```
3) panel: per-pod heatmap of pod:gpu_queue_p99:rate5m and overlay of pool:gpu_saturation:ratio

mike: Note: older Prometheus versions don't support instant vector functions like quantile_over_time. safer to implement as recording rules and then query the recordings in Grafana. Also add max_over_time(recording[10m]) to catch bursts.

kai: Also correlate K8s probe failures and node egress errors:
```
sum(increase(kubelet_probe_failures_total[5m])) by (node)
sum(increase(nginx_upstream_responses_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) by (upstream)
```
I saw small probe flaps on apac-nodes-* around the windows.

devon: Operational plan & cost posture: if we need immediate headroom we can scale apac reserved pools +2 nodes temporarily. estimate: ~+$11k/month. prefer to avoid churn if this is a transient network regression.

jordyn: Logs correlate: LB 502 spikes -> client retries -> request bursts -> batch windows inflate -> p99 latency jumps. root seems to be egress LB errors.

mike: Proposed runbook items:
- Add the recording rules (pod:gpu_queue_p99:rate5m, pool:gpu_saturation:ratio)
- Update Grafana to show per-pod p99, pool saturation, and LB error overlay
- Add composite alert that pages if pool:gpu_saturation:ratio > 0.9 sustained 10m AND max(pod:gpu_queue_p99) > 200ms
- Short-term automated scale: if composite alert triggers for 15m, auto-scale apac pools +2 with a 30m cooldown and annotated cost delta

ana: I'll open a PR with recording rules + dashboard updates and include panels that are explicit about the LB 5xxs overlayed. tagging @mike @jordyn for review.

sre-bot: Incident draft created: INC-20250818-APAC-EGRESS-DRIFT. Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-20250818-APAC-EGRESS-DRIFT

devon: For the PR include: rollout steps, rollback, cost delta, and automation cooldown. If we auto-scale, ensure we have an explicit cleanup job.

kai: Also add a staging chaos test: simulate egress packet loss / increased RTT to upstream LB and verify recording rules and composite alert trigger. add to ci-nightly.

ana: PR incoming in ~40m. I'll attach grafana snapshots, sliced logs, and the probe failure queries. will also note the estimated monthly cost if scaling is needed.

mike: :thumbsup: ping me when PR is up. I'll run the staging chaos and approve if metrics and alerting behave.
